title-group.article-title: Real-world effectiveness of osimertinib in EGFR-mutated metastatic non-small cell lung cancer.

contrib-group.aff: Central Oncology Research Hospital, Houston, TX
Westlake Comprehensive Cancer Center, Seattle, WA
Harborview Institute of Oncology, San Diego, CA

permissions.copyright-statement: © 2026 by American Society of Clinical Oncology

abstract.p: Background: The effectiveness of osimertinib outside clinical trials remains incompletely characterized for EGFR-mutated metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. We evaluated treatment patterns, clinical outcomes, and safety in a multi-institutional real-world cohort. Methods: We retrospectively identified consecutive adults with EGFR-mutated metastatic non-small cell lung cancer who initiated osimertinib between 2020 and 2025 across six oncology centers. Demographic, clinicopathologic, treatment, and outcome data were abstracted from electronic records using a common data model. The primary endpoint was real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS); secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), overall survival (OS), treatment duration, and grade 3 or higher adverse events. Time-to-event outcomes were estimated using Kaplan–Meier methods. Results: The analysis included 341 patients with a median age of 67 years; 64% were female and the median number of prior systemic treatment lines was one. After a median follow-up of 22.1 months, ORR was 61.8%, median rwPFS was 14.6 months, and median OS was 30.8 months. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 18.7% of patients. Pneumonitis was documented in 3.8%. In exploratory subgroup analysis, patients with exon 19 deletion had a median rwPFS of 16.1 months. Conclusions: In routine practice, osimertinib demonstrated clinically meaningful activity in EGFR-mutated metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, with outcomes generally consistent with its established treatment role. Toxicity remained manageable, although monitoring for pneumonitis is warranted. These findings support continued real-world evaluation in broader and underrepresented patient populations. Research Sponsor: None.
